paragraphs: Zophar asks Job, "Can you fathom the deep things of God or discover the limits of the Almighty?" (Job 11:7). He says those things are higher than the heavens and deeper than Sheol (Job 11:8). That's a big picture of God, friend, and it's a good reminder that He is bigger than anything we can measure. I can't even measure my own cookie planet without running out of tape.

But I think Zophar takes that bigness and makes it a tidy formula. Put away the iniquity, he says, and "Your life will be brighter than noonday" (Job 11:14, 17). I think Zophar had his answer ready before Job even finished hurting. Big on God's mystery, small on the hug.

So here's what I'm taking from this one, baker. When someone is hurting, be quick to listen and slow to hand them a neat explanation. Zophar did point Job toward lifting up his hands to God (Job 11:13), and that's a good place for any hurting heart to go. Job's story isn't over, friend, and this conversation is far from finished.
